name: List
grades: A: no errors and at most 1 warning. B: no errors. C: 1 error. D: 2 errors. F: 3 or more. Each rule counts once, however many places it fires. Hints never count.

1.name: Title at the top, in the bar or as a large title

2.name: Back arrow, close X, Done or Edit at the top

3.name: One thing at the right end of each row

4.name: Thumbnail, icon or avatar at the left of each row

5.name: Two-line rows: a name with a pale detail line

6.name: Way to add: a plus, a create button or a compose icon

9.name: Empty message or an Empty slot

10.name: Section headings that group the rows

v1.name: Media and file rows
expect: A thumbnail, icon or avatar at the left of every row
A name with a pale detail line in every row
A button, value or chevron at the right end of the rows

v3.name: Grouped rows
expect: Section headings that split the rows into groups
A button, value or chevron at the right end of the rows
A thumbnail, icon or avatar at the left of most rows

v4.name: Empty list
expect: An empty message or an empty slot in the page
A back, close, Done or Edit control at the top
No rows, so no thumbnails or right-end controls

not_checked: What happens after a tap on a row or on the way to add: one screen cannot show it.
Whether the list scrolls, loads more rows or refreshes: one screen shows one moment.
Whether the way to add is easy to find: many lists are read-only, so a missing add control is not graded.
Contrast of the pale detail line under each row name: it is pale on purpose, so only the title and the empty message are measured.

rules.says: The page is empty and gives a message but no button to start.
rules.why: An empty page gives a message and no button. Seen on 10 of 62 checked screens.

rules.says: A popover, a toast or a floating button sits on top of the rows.
rules.why: A popover, a toast or a floating button covers rows of the list. Seen on 5 of 62 checked screens.

rules.says: A row name is cut off with an ellipsis, so it cannot be read in full.
rules.why: Row text is cut off with an ellipsis, so the full name cannot be read. Seen on 9 of 62 checked screens.

rules.says: Text or a close control is too faint against what is behind it.
rules.why: Accessibility guidelines ask for 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text: 18 pt, or 14 pt bold (button labels are bold). Controls, such as a close or back glyph, need 3:1. Below 3:1 is an error; from 3:1 to 4.5:1 on smaller text it is a warning. Checked on the labels of buttons, the lines of the parts marked as key text, and the close and back glyphs. Not checked on a dimmed screen or over a photo or a pattern, or on the label of a greyed-out button (the guidelines leave out controls that cannot be used yet). Faint placeholder text in an empty field is only a hint, since iOS's own placeholder grey is about 1.7:1.

rules.says: Text is smaller than 11 pt.
rules.why: Apple lists 11 pt as the smallest text size on iOS. Measured from the height of each line, so it is about right, not exact. Checked on the parts marked as key text.

rules.says: A control sits under the status bar or the home indicator.
rules.why: The status bar row at the top and the bottom 34 pt, where the home indicator sits, belong to the system on phones without a home button. Flagged when a control reaches the status bar row or comes within 17 pt of the bottom edge, so a button that only touches the area is not counted.

rules.says: A close or back control is drawn smaller than 13 pt.
rules.why: Apple asks for a 44 x 44 pt tap area. The standard close X in a bar is drawn about 13 to 17 pt across inside that area, so only a smaller drawing is flagged. A screenshot cannot show the tap area itself, so this is a hint.
